lessons.title: A Map for Everyone
lessons.goal: 找出問題，判斷哪個修改真正有幫助
lessons.story:
[Library volunteer chat, Wednesday]
Nina: Our new library map is ready. I used green for the reading area and red for the computer area. What do you think?
Eric: The colors look nice, but I printed the map in black and white. Both areas look almost the same.
Nina: I did not think about that. Should I use brighter colors?
Eric: Colors alone may not solve it. Could we add a book symbol to the reading area and a computer symbol to the computer area?
Nina: Yes, and I can write the area names below the symbols.
Eric: Great. My little brother is still learning to read. The pictures will help him too.
Nina: I will update the map before we put it near the entrance tomorrow.
Eric: Let’s print one more copy in black and white first. That way, we can check whether everyone can follow it.

words.example: The library has a quiet reading area.
A book symbol marks the reading area.
The map is near the entrance.
Brighter colors may not solve the problem.
The symbols make the map easier to follow.

options: The library has no computers.
The two areas look similar on a black-and-white copy.
The map is too small to print.
The entrance is in the wrong place.
questions.explanation: Eric 印成黑白後，原本不同顏色的兩區看起來很像，這才是要解決的問題。
questions.evidence: Both areas look almost the same.

questions.prompt: What changes will Nina make to the map?
options: Remove every color and picture.
Move the computer area outside.
Print it only in green.
Add symbols and area names.
questions.explanation: Eric 建議圖示，Nina 接著補上區域名稱；兩個修改合起來就是 D。
questions.evidence: Yes, and I can write the area names below the symbols.

questions.prompt: Why does Eric want another black-and-white copy before using the map?
options: To check whether the changes solve the original problem.
To count how many books the library owns.
To keep Nina from finishing the map.
To make the colors even brighter.
questions.explanation: 第一次的問題是在黑白列印後才出現，所以用同樣方式再測一次，能確認修正有沒有用。
questions.evidence: Let’s print one more copy in black and white first.

questions.prompt: Detective: What does “follow” mean in the last sentence?
options: Walk behind a volunteer.
Copy the same colors.
Understand the map and use its directions.
Wait for someone at the entrance.
questions.explanation: 前文在討論地圖是否好懂，因此 follow it 指看懂並依照地圖找路。
questions.evidence: That way, we can check whether everyone can follow it.

questions.prompt: Who else may benefit from the picture symbols, according to Eric?
options: People who want to buy a printer.
Young children who are still learning to read.
Students who want a larger computer screen.
Volunteers who already know every room.
questions.explanation: Eric 提到弟弟正在學閱讀，圖示也會幫到他；圖示能補足文字閱讀能力的限制。
questions.evidence: My little brother is still learning to read. The pictures will help him too.

questions.prompt: Which idea best describes the team’s approach?
options: A beautiful map never needs to be tested.
Only experienced readers should use library maps.
Printing more copies always fixes a design problem.
Useful information should remain clear in different situations.
questions.explanation: 他們考量黑白列印和還不熟文字的小讀者，改善符號與文字，再檢驗成果，重點是不同使用情況下都要清楚。
questions.evidence: Colors alone may not solve it.
